The following synthetic pathway of a pyrimidine, cytidine 5' triphosphate, CTP, begins with the condensation of two small molecules by the enzyme, aspartate transcarbamylase (ATCase).

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: the figure shows the CTP biosynthesis pathway. The top of the pathway starts with carbamoyl phosphate and aspartic acid, and the enzyme aspartate transcarbamylase (ATCase) is labeled beside an early step. The pathway generates intermediate products downward in sequence, and the final product at the bottom is labeled Cytidine 5'-triphosphate (CTP). There is also a feedback arrow in the figure returning from near the bottom CTP to the starting ATCase region of the pathway, with the label “High CTP” beside the arrow. Reasoning: this feedback indicates that when the CTP level is high, it will feedback inhibit the early ATCase step, thereby reducing pathway flux. The question asks about the situation when the CTP level in the cell is low; low CTP means this high-CTP feedback inhibition is weakened or removed, so more metabolites will flow downward along this biosynthetic pathway.

Apply negative-feedback logic: if high CTP inhibits early pathway traffic, low CTP removes the inhibitory feedback, so metabolic traffic down the pathway increases.
